title: pi-xfer mesh config
description: Configuration for pi-xfer's mesh transport, stored at ~/.pi/xfer/mesh.config.json. Adding a "$schema" key pointing at this file gives key completion and validation in editors that speak JSON Schema. pi-xfer itself ignores unknown keys, so "$schema" is harmless at runtime.

$schema.description: Optional editor hint. Point it at this schema's raw URL for completion and validation; pi-xfer ignores it.

endpoint.description: Control-plane URL of the mesh engine — a plain literal. Credentials inside the URL (https://namespace:token@host) are refused: put the namespace in "namespace" and the token in "token". Can be self-hosted (http://host:6420) or Rivet Cloud (https://api.rivet.dev).

namespace.description: Isolated environment your nodes live in. A literal or a $ENV_VAR reference; a leading "!command" is rejected here — a namespace is a short identifier and does not need a command. Defaults to the engine-side "default".

token.description: Auth token for the engine (an sk_… API key from Rivet Cloud, or the admin token on a self-hosted engine), sent as an Authorization: Bearer header. Three forms, the same as apiKey in pi's models.json: a literal; $NAME or ${NAME} environment interpolation ($$ and $! escape a literal $ and !); or a leading !command, whose trimmed stdout is used. A command runs through a shell each time the mesh talks to the engine and is not cached, so a rotated secret is picked up on the next operation. An unset $VAR is an error, never an empty token. Security: a !command executes with your own permissions, so write permission on this file is equivalent to permission to execute code as you — keep it 0600 and out of any repository.

pool.description: Envoy/runner pool this host's runners join (the machine or host name on a mixed fleet), so the engine can only schedule this Node's actor onto this machine. Unset = the engine-wide default pool, where the engine may place the actor on any host. An existing actor does not move pools by itself.
